title: 韓国の保守勢力が壊滅の危機　統一地方選ひかえ迷走、牙城も揺れる
extracted_text:
韓国の李在明（イ・ジェミョン）政権下で初の大型選挙となる統一地方選挙が、1カ月後に迫る。李政権を支える革新（進歩）系与党が高い支持率を維持する一方、保守系野党は全く振るわない。尹錫悦（ユン・ソンニョル）前大統領の弾劾の衝撃を引きずっているためで、「保守の牙城」とされる地域まで陥落の危機にさらされている。

4月下旬のお昼時、ソウル市長の呉世勲（オ・セフン）氏は休憩中の会社員が行き交うソウルの街中をスーツ姿で練り歩いていた。

6月3日投開票のソウル市長選で5選を狙う呉氏は、最大野党「国民の力」の有力な次期大統領候補の一人。逆風の選挙戦を見越してか、一般市民の前では保守のトレードマークである赤いジャンパーを極力着ないようにしているようだ。

李大統領は呉氏の対抗馬として、かねて目をかけてきたソウル市城東区長の鄭愿伍（チョン・ウォノ）氏を与党「共に民主党」の候補に選んだ。最新の世論調査で鄭氏は10ポイントほど呉氏をリードする。

現職であっても、保守の看板を掲げる限り向かい風にさらされるのが今回の地方選だ。韓国第2の都市、釜山でも国民の力の現職が、共に民主党の送り込んだ元海洋水産相の候補と横一線で並ぶ。

2022年の前回地方選は保守の圧勝だった。尹政権が発足から1カ月弱の時期で、主要17地域の首長選のうち12を国民の力が押さえた。一部地域の統合により16地域となる今回の首長選で、保守は伝統的に強い南東部の慶尚道を死守しようとしている。

ソウル地裁は2月、大統領を弾劾され内乱首謀罪で起訴された尹氏に無期懲役の判決を下した。ソウル市内では今も週末ごとに中国排斥など過激な主張とともに「ユン・アゲイン（尹復活）」を叫ぶ人たちのデモ行進が続く。

こうした支持者を抱える国民の力の執行部は、尹氏による戒厳が明確に誤りだったと総括しておらず、中道に近い支持層の離反を招いた。

党を率いる張東赫（チャン・ドンヒョク）代表は1月に尹氏の弾劾訴追を推進した前代表の韓東勲（ハン・ドンフン）氏を除名し、党内の亀裂は広がった。韓国ギャラップの調査で国民の力の支持率は20%と、共に民主党との差は30ポイント近い。

保守系の元韓国政府高官は「このままでは国政と地方の両方で保守の影響力が失われてしまう。有権者がバランス感覚を働かせることに期待するしかない」と話す。

保守の意地は第3の都市、大邱（テグ）市長選で試されることになる。軍事独裁を敷いた朴正熙（パク・チョンヒ）元大統領の出身地で、多くの保守政治家を輩出してきた。

共に民主党はこの保守の岩盤に早ばやと元首相の金富謙（キム・ブギョム）氏を擁立した。金氏の政治スタンスは穏健な保守に近く、中道の市民を引き寄せようという狙いは明らかだ。

国民の力は対抗馬として、尹氏のもとで経済副首相を務めた秋慶鎬（チュ・ギョンホ）氏を選んだ。非常戒厳の直後、国会による解除決議の採決を妨害しようとした罪で在宅起訴されている。「尹カラー」の濃い人物で正面突破をはかる戦略だが、今回ばかりは拒否感を示す市民が少なくないとみられる。

地方選のタイミングとほぼ同じくして就任1年を迎える李在明大統領の直近の支持率は67%（韓国ギャラップ）だった。就任直後の64%から高水準を保つ。

李氏は地方首長の時代から世論を先読みするような素早い実行力に定評がある。「人工知能（AI）3大強国入り」を掲げ、株式相場を味方につけた。韓国の総合株価指数（KOSPI）は最高値を更新し続け、政権発足来の上昇幅は2.4倍に達している。

米国のイラン攻撃に伴う中東情勢の混迷でも、巨大与党を動かして総額26.2兆ウォン（約2兆8000億円）の補正予算を成立させるなど野党に批判の隙を与えていない。韓国政治の今の構図は、高市早苗首相の人気を背景に巨大与党が生まれた日本の政治環境と、左右は逆だがよく似ている。

韓国の地方選の結果は日本に影響するだろうか。革新系勢力には1980年代の学生運動経験者が多く残る。米国依存からの脱却、北朝鮮との関係改善、日本との歴史問題といった課題に関心を持つ彼らの政治的な基盤が一段と強まれば、政権の外交姿勢や安全保障政策に変化が生まれる可能性がある。

translated_text:
The unified local elections, the first major election under the Lee Jae-myung administration, are now just one month away. While the progressive ruling party supporting the Lee administration maintains high approval ratings, the conservative opposition parties are not performing at all. This is because they are still dealing with the shock of former President Yoon Suk Yeol's impeachment, and even regions considered 'conservative strongholds' are now at risk of falling.

In late April around lunchtime, Seoul Mayor Oh Se-hoon was walking through the streets of Seoul in a suit, blending in with office workers coming and going during their breaks.

Oh, who is aiming for a fifth term as Seoul mayor in the June 3rd election, is one of the leading presidential candidates for the main opposition party, People's Power Party. Perhaps anticipating a challenging election, he appears to avoid wearing the signature red jacket associated with conservatives when in front of ordinary citizens.

President Lee has chosen Seoul Seongdong-gu District Chief Chung Won-woo as the candidate from the ruling Democratic Party, someone he has long supported. In the latest polls, Chung leads Oh by about 10 points.

Even incumbents face headwinds if they champion the conservative banner in this local election. In Busan, South Korea's second-largest city, the People's Power Party incumbent is in a tight race with a former海洋水產部長 (Minister of Oceans and Fisheries) candidate fielded by the Democratic Party.

Conservatives won decisively in the previous local elections in 2022. Within a month of the Yoon administration taking office, People's Power Party captured 12 of 17 regional mayoral positions. In this election, where the number has been reduced to 16 due to some regional mergers, conservatives are trying to hold onto Gyeongsang Province in the southeast, where they have traditionally been strong.

In February, the Seoul Central District Court sentenced Yoon, who was impeached as president and indicted for rebellion, to life imprisonment. In Seoul, demonstrations continue every weekend with protesters shouting 'Yoon Revival' along with extreme anti-China slogans.

The leadership of People's Power Party, which backs these supporters, has not acknowledged that Yoon's martial law declaration was clearly wrong, causing centrist supporters to abandon the party.

Party leader Chang Dong-hyuk expelled former leader Han Dong-hoon in January, who had pushed for Yoon's impeachment prosecution, widening the factional rift within the party. According to a Gallup Korea poll, People's Power Party's approval rating stands at 20%, nearly 30 points behind the Democratic Party.

A former conservative government official said, 'As things stand, conservative influence will be lost in both national and local governance. We can only hope that voters will use their judgment to maintain balance.'

Conservative pride will be tested in the Daegu mayoral election, the third-largest city. Daegu is the hometown of former President Park Chung-hee, who established a military dictatorship, and has produced many conservative politicians.

The Democratic Party has quickly nominated former Prime Minister Kim Boo-kyum for this conservative stronghold. Kim's political stance is close to moderate conservative, clearly attempting to attract centrist voters.

People's Power Party has chosen Choo Kyung-ho, who served as Deputy Prime Minister for Economic Affairs under Yoon, as their rival candidate. He is currently under house arrest for attempting to obstruct the National Assembly's vote to lift the emergency martial law. As a prominent 'Yoon loyalist,' they are attempting a direct assault, but there are believed to be many citizens who are unwilling to support this approach.

President Lee Jae-myung, who is approaching one year in office, currently has an approval rating of 67% (Gallup Korea), maintaining high levels since the 64% he had just after taking office.

Lee is known for his quick execution ability, often reading public opinion first even during his time as a local mayor. By committing to making South Korea 'one of the top three AI powers,' he won over the stock market. The KOSPI continues to reach record highs, with stock values rising 2.4 times since the administration took office.

Even amid the Middle East turmoil following the US attack on Iran, the large ruling party pushed through a supplementary budget totaling 26.2 trillion won (about 2.8 trillion yen), leaving no opening for opposition criticism. South Korea's current political landscape closely resembles Japan's, where a large ruling party emerged based on the popularity of Prime Minister Sanna Ishi, though the political alignments are reversed.

Will the results of South Korea's local elections affect Japan? Many progressive supporters remain from the 1980s student movement era. If their political base strengthens further—with their focus on reducing dependence on the US, improving relations with North Korea, and addressing historical issues with Japan—changes could arise in the administration's foreign policy and security posture.
title_en: South Korea's Conservative Forces Face Annihilation Crisis as Local Elections Approach, Even Strongholds Shaking
